repairs.gloss: free from flaw or blemish or impurity
repairs.current_note: Goes beyond flaws and marks to anything mixed in that spoils it, so it can describe a substance, not only a performance.
repairs.reader_said: tone_lint, rule narrowing, matched "describe a substance, not": do not restrict the sense further than the gloss does
repairs.axis: no fault found in it → complete and consummate perfection
examples: the clear complexion of a healthy young woman

whole_family.gloss: being complete of its kind and without defect or blemish
whole_family.tone: The unqualified standard here, claiming completeness of its kind as well as the absence of blemish, where *flawless* claims only the absence.

whole_family.gloss: (of a record) having no marks of discredit or offense
whole_family.tone: Praise by absence - a record with nothing marked against it, a narrower claim than the completeness *perfect* asserts.

whole_family.gloss: free from flaw or blemish or impurity
whole_family.tone: Goes beyond flaws and marks to anything mixed in that spoils it, so it can describe a substance, not only a performance.
Perfection as drilled familiarity - the thing is known so thoroughly that error does not arise, where *errorless* only reports that none did.

whole_family.gloss: perfect and complete in every respect; having all necessary qualities
whole_family.tone: Asserts that every necessary quality is present, the opposite test from *flawless*: nothing missing rather than nothing wrong.

whole_family.gloss: perfect and complete in every respect; having all necessary qualities
whole_family.tone: Formal where *complete* is plain, and it turns having every needed quality into the highest kind of praise.
Puts the perfection in the grasp rather than in the thing - the understanding is finished, and it says so flatly.
The idiom tightens *down* into exactness: not merely understood but understood to the letter.
Dignifies the same perfect understanding as an attainment, where *down* merely reports the state.
A flat count of no errors, the coolest word in the family beside *impeccable*'s admiration.
Takes in fault as well as error, so it acquits the conduct and not just the execution.
Lifts the same absence of fault into something untouched, admiring where *errorless* is merely accurate.
Reads the absence of fault as a standard held to - admiration rather than measurement.
Treats being without fault as something kept whole rather than achieved, and sounds stiffer than *faultless*.
Single-minded - one flaw would undo it, where *complete* asks instead whether everything is there.
Simply says there is no flaw, without the admiration that *flawless* carries.

repairs.gloss: arising from or marked by despair or loss of hope
repairs.current_note: Points at the despair itself, whether a thing comes from lost hope or just shows it, where *hopeless* points at the chances.
repairs.reader_said: tone_lint, rule etymology, matched "comes from": drop the origin story unless it has been checked against a source
repairs.axis: faint hope still left → hope wholly gone and the collapse showing
examples: a despairing view of the world situation
the last despairing plea of the condemned criminal

synset_siblings.tone: The straining side of the same despair — something arising from lost hope rather than merely showing it, so it pushes where *despairing* only mourns.

whole_family.gloss: without hope because there seems to be no possibility of comfort or success
whole_family.tone: The plain verdict: no hope because no comfort or success looks possible - about the odds, where *despairing* is about the feeling.
The most degrading member: utter resignation or hopelessness worn openly, so that the giving-up is itself what gets judged.
Simply “not hopeful”: the same utter resignation or hopelessness as *abject*, but without the scorn, saying less than it means.
Paints the little-or-no hope rather than measuring it, and paints it unrelieved, which is what puts it past *dim*.
The same shortage of hope felt as bareness and exposure rather than as the darkness of *black*.
The mildest of the three, since it sits on the “little” rather than the “no” — hope faint but not yet out.

whole_family.gloss: arising from or marked by despair or loss of hope
whole_family.tone: Points at the despair itself, whether a thing comes from lost hope or just shows it, where *hopeless* points at the chances.

whole_family.gloss: arising from or marked by despair or loss of hope
whole_family.tone: The straining side of the same despair — something arising from lost hope rather than merely showing it, so it pushes where *despairing* only mourns.
A sunk, settled state with hope gone or all but gone, heavier than *dim* and far quieter than *desperate*.
Puts that same absent-or-nearly-absent hope in the body, a sickness felt rather than the low weight of *despondent*.
Hopelessness that is marked or shown in a way inviting pity, not the reproach *abject* invites.

whole_family.gloss: having no prospect or hope of a future
whole_family.tone: Turns the loss forward — neither prospect nor hope of a future — a flat structural verdict beside the mood of *forlorn*.
Two failures at once, unable to function and no help at hand, so it sounds like a plea, not *hopeless*'s verdict.
Unable to function and without help, like *helpless*, but as a settled state rather than a moment, so it sounds beyond rescue.
Aimed at the problem, not at anyone: a flat statement that no solution can be hoped for, with no blame in it.

repairs.gloss: free from favoritism or self-interest or bias or deception; conforming with established standards or rules
repairs.current_note: Plain approval no one can argue with: it confirms nobody was favored or tricked, without the weight of principle *just* carries.
repairs.reader_said: tone_lint, rule hedge-claim, matched "no one can": a claim about all speakers is a distribution claim in disguise
repairs.axis: neutral naming of rules against unfair dealing → emphatic praise for dealing fairly

synset_siblings.tone: Heavier than *fair* - the same absence of bias, but weighted as a standard rightly upheld rather than a condition merely met.

whole_family.gloss: free from favoritism or self-interest or bias or deception; conforming with established standards or rules

whole_family.gloss: of laws and regulations; designed to protect trade and commerce from unfair business practices
whole_family.tone: Technical and as neutral as *antimonopoly*, marking a regulation's protective purpose rather than approving anybody's conduct.

whole_family.gloss: exhibiting or calling for sportsmanship or fair play
whole_family.tone: Praises by what is missing - nothing foul in the play - where *sportsmanlike* names the good quality directly.

whole_family.gloss: exhibiting or calling for sportsmanship or fair play
whole_family.tone: Warmer and easier than *clean*, crediting fair play as a spirit brought to the contest rather than a rule left unbroken.

whole_family.gloss: exhibiting or calling for sportsmanship or fair play
whole_family.tone: The most casual of these, informal and light, granting the same approval with none of *sportsmanlike*'s weight.

whole_family.gloss: exhibiting or calling for sportsmanship or fair play
whole_family.tone: The formal member - it measures conduct against a named standard of sportsmanship instead of merely reporting, as *clean* does, that nothing foul happened.

whole_family.gloss: of a person; just and impartial; not prejudiced
whole_family.tone: Praises a settled cast of mind rather than a single dealing - the impartiality is lodged in the person.
The emphatic one - its doubled phrasing insists there is nothing left to question, where *just* simply states that the standard was met.

whole_family.gloss: of or characteristic of low rank or importance
whole_family.tone: Puts a thing below others and lets that ranking carry the sting, where *humble* names the same low place without ranking it.

whole_family.gloss: low or inferior in station or quality
whole_family.tone: Names low station with a quiet grace, so the lowness reads as unpretending rather than deficient.

whole_family.gloss: low or inferior in station or quality
whole_family.tone: The blunt monosyllable for that station, stating the bottom position flatly and with none of the softening in *humble*.

whole_family.gloss: low or inferior in station or quality

whole_family.gloss: low or inferior in station or quality
whole_family.tone: The tactful word for the same lowness, declining to call it poor and leaving the thing its dignity.

whole_family.gloss: low or inferior in station or quality
whole_family.tone: Shrinks rather than ranks: the low quality comes across as being unimportant, not as a place on a ladder.

whole_family.gloss: fairly poor to not very good
whole_family.tone: Damns by withholding: it refuses praise rather than delivering a charge, and the refusal is the verdict.

whole_family.gloss: at a low level in rank or importance
whole_family.tone: Purely positional, marking a rung on a scale of rank without judging the worth of whatever stands there.
A coordinate rather than a verdict, fixing a point between top and bottom and claiming nothing about quality.

whole_family.gloss: decisively surpassed by something else so as to appear to be of a lower class
whole_family.tone: The strongest here: the low standing comes from a contest clearly lost, and carries the humiliation of the comparison.

repairs.current_note: Simply states where someone stands - there is no one to answer to, and the person is not judged for it.

repairs.axis: irresponsibility indulged as charm → irresponsibility condemned as unfitness

whole_family.gloss: showing lack of care for consequences
whole_family.tone: The plain charge the rest take their colour from - blame falls on the consequences left unweighed, with none of the cheer of *carefree*.
The most forgiving word here - the missing care reads as freedom from burden rather than neglect of duty.
Showy boldness rather than lightness - it shows off not caring, where *carefree* simply has no worry to shed.
Motion with the brakes off - it approves the ease while leaving the absent check audible.
Indulgent - it credits a temperament rather than charging a fault.
Its sing-song rhyme makes the cheer sound silly and disorganized, tipping into criticism where *happy-go-lucky* stays fond.
The cheer here undercuts the person as giddy and unfit to be trusted, where *carefree* leaves them intact.

whole_family.gloss: characterized by inability or unwillingness to work toward a goal or assume responsibility
whole_family.tone: Flatly dismissive - it writes someone off by what they never get done, with no charm allowed into the failing.
A verdict of unfitness rather than a report of behaviour, and the most withering word in the set.

whole_family.gloss: lacking a sense of restraint or responsibility
whole_family.tone: A light word for the fault - what is missing is restraint, not any active wrongdoing.

whole_family.gloss: lacking a sense of restraint or responsibility
whole_family.tone: Carries a moral edge *idle* does not - the restraint gone slack is the kind a person is expected to hold.

whole_family.gloss: irresponsible in the use of firearms
whole_family.tone: The cheerful *-happy* ending set against carelessness with a gun is the whole sting of it.
Simply states where someone stands - there is no one to answer to, and the person is not judged for it.
Judged from outside - where *irresponsible* looks at the consequences, this looks at whoever was depending.

repairs.current_note: The flat, basic word: it says only that the thing was not noticed, blaming no one and giving it no claim on attention.
repairs.reader_said: tone_lint, rule hedge-claim, matched "no one and": a claim about all speakers is a distribution claim in disguise
repairs.axis: bare absence of notice → attention withheld from something with a claim on it
examples: hoped his departure had passed unnoticed

whole_family.tone: The flat, basic word: it says only that the thing was not noticed, blaming no one and giving it no claim on attention.
In this sense the passing-over is accidental, so the word marks a lapse rather than a snub.
The same accidental slip as *disregarded*, but implying the thing once held attention and lost it, leaving it a little less important.
The one where withholding attention reads as chosen - a snub rather than an oversight, and the sting sits in that choice.
Puts the weight on attention that was owed and not paid, so it carries a sense of duty unmet that *ignored* does not.
The mildest of the three: something was there to attend to, without *ignored*'s choice or *neglected*'s failure of care.
A miss rather than a refusal - it concedes that the thing should have entered the reckoning and quietly admits the error.
Flat where *overlooked* is apologetic: it says only that nothing was made of the thing, conceding no mistake.
The barest of the three - the plain negative of taking something into account, with no suggestion that anyone should have.
Carries the shadow of someone who might have noticed, so it can be a relief as easily as a slight.
Flatly sensory beside *unobserved* - nothing registered, with no watcher implied for the thing to have escaped.
Formal and abstract, covering both not noticing a thing and saying nothing of it, with the weight on the noticing.
Leans the other way from *unperceived*: the thing may well have been seen, and the point is that nothing was said of it.
